questions.problem:
Calculate the area ${A}_{△}$ of the triangle spanned by $p=⟨0,5,-1⟩$ and $q=⟨6,0,1⟩.$

${A}_{△}=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p\times q & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 5 & -1 \\ 6 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(5\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 0)i-(0\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 6)j+(0\cdot 0-5\cdot 6)k \\  & =5i-6j-30k \\  & =⟨5,-6,-30⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,p\times q\,| \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-6)^{2}+(-30)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+36+900} \\  & =\sqrt{961} \\  & =31.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{31}{2}.
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & -4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -2 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot (-4))i-(2\cdot 0-(-2)\cdot (-4))j+(2\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 2)k \\  & =-4i+8j+2k \\  & =⟨-4,8,2⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{8}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{84} \\  & =2\sqrt{21}.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Calculate the length of the altitude $VL$ of the $△\,TUV$, if $T(1,0,1)$, $U(3,2,-1)$, $V(-1,1,0).$

$VL=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $VL$ can be related to the area of $△\,TUV$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}VL\cdot TU
$$

So, to find $VL,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{TU}$ and $\overset{\to }{TV}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TU} & =u-t \\  & =(3i+2j-k)-(i+k) \\  & =2i+2j-2k \\  & =⟨2,2,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{TV} & =v-t \\  & =(-i+j)-(i+k) \\  & =-2i+j-k \\  & =⟨-2,1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TU}\times \overset{\to }{TV} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot 1)i-(2\cdot (-1)-(-2)\cdot (-2))j+(2\cdot 1-2\cdot (-2))k \\  & =0i+6j+6k \\  & =⟨0,6,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{TU}$ and $\overset{\to }{TV}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{TU}\times \overset{\to }{TV}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{6}^{2}+{6}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{72} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,TUV$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{2}=3\sqrt{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $TU$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}TU & =|\overset{\to }{TU}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}VL\cdot TU,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}VL\cdot TU \\ 3\sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}VL\cdot 2\sqrt{3} \\ 3\sqrt{2} & =VL\cdot \sqrt{3} \\ VL & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ VL & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}TK\cdot RS
$$

So, to find $TK,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{RS}$ and $\overset{\to }{RT}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{RS} & =s-r \\  & =(7i+4j+5k)-(4i+5j+6k) \\  & =3i-j-k \\  & =⟨3,-1,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{RT} & =t-r \\  & =(6i+8j+4k)-(4i+5j+6k) \\  & =2i+3j-2k \\  & =⟨2,3,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{RS}\times \overset{\to }{RT} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)(-2)-(-1)\cdot 3)i-(3(-2)-(-1)\cdot 2)j+(3\cdot 3-(-1)\cdot 2)k \\  & =5i+4j+11k \\  & =⟨5,4,11⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{RS}$ and $\overset{\to }{RT}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{RS}\times \overset{\to }{RT}| \\  & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{11}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{162} \\  & =9\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,RST$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $RS$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}RS & =|\overset{\to }{RS}| \\  & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}TK\cdot RS,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}TK\cdot \sqrt{11} \\ TK & =\frac{9\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{11}} \\ TK & =\frac{9\sqrt{22}}{11}.\end{aligned}

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -4 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 \\ -2 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-2)\cdot 3-2\cdot 3)i-((-4)\cdot 3-(-2)\cdot 3)j+((-4)\cdot 2-(-2)\cdot (-2))k \\  & =-12i+6j-12k \\  & =⟨-12,6,-12⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-12)^{2}+{6}^{2}+(-12)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{324} \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{18}{2}=9.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{29}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ 9 & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot \sqrt{29} \\ 18 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{29} \\ CH & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{29}} \\ CH & =\frac{18\sqrt{29}}{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $VH$ of the $△\,TUV$, if $T(3,2,3)$, $U(0,1,0)$, $V(2,1,2).$
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $VH$ can be related to the area of $△\,TUV$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}VH\cdot TU
$$

So, to find $VH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{TU}$ and $\overset{\to }{TV}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TU} & =u-t \\  & =j-(3i+2j+3k) \\  & =-3i-j-3k \\  & =⟨-3,-1,-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{TV} & =v-t \\  & =(2i+j+2k)-(3i+2j+3k) \\  & =-i-j-k \\  & =⟨-1,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{TU}\times \overset{\to }{TV} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot (-3))i-((-3)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot (-3))j+((-3)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot (-1))k \\  & =-2i+2k \\  & =⟨-2,0,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{TU}$ and $\overset{\to }{TV}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{TU}\times \overset{\to }{TV}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,TUV$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2}=\sqrt{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $TU$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}TU & =|\overset{\to }{TU}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{19}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}VH\cdot TU,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}VH\cdot TU \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{1}{2}VH\cdot \sqrt{19} \\ 2\sqrt{2} & =VH\cdot \sqrt{19} \\ VH & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{19}} \\ VH & =\frac{2\sqrt{38}}{19}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Triangle Spanned by Two Vectors
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the area of the triangle spanned by $\mathbf{a}=\langle 4,0,-3 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-1,2 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 0 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-1))i-(4\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot 5)j+(4\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 5)k \\  & =-3i-23j-4k \\  & =⟨-3,-23,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,a\times b\,| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-23)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{554}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is

$$
A_{\triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{\sqrt{554}}{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the area of the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC,$ if $A(1,0,-2),$ $B(-2,0,1),$ $C(1,1,-1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-2i+k)-(i-2k) \\  & =-3i+3k \\  & =⟨-3,0,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i+j-k)-(i-2k) \\  & =j+k \\  & =⟨0,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-3\cdot 1)i-(-3\cdot 1-3\cdot 0)j+(-3\cdot 1-0\cdot 0)k \\  & =-3i+3j-3k \\  & =⟨-3,3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ is

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ if $A(-1,1,0),$ $B(1,1,2),$ $C(1,-1,1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude (height) can be related to the area of the triangle as follows:

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{b \cdot h}{2},
$$

 
where $b$ is a base and $h$ is the corresponding altitude of the triangle.

For the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC,$ we have $h=CH,$ and $b=AB.$ So, we have

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB.
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find $A_{\bigtriangleup}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(i+j+2k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i+2k \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-j+k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i-2j+k \\  & =⟨2,-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-2\cdot (-2))i-(2\cdot 1-2\cdot 2)j+(2\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 2)k \\  & =4i+2j-4k \\  & =⟨4,2,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ is

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 = 3.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula $A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot 2\sqrt{2} \\ 3 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{2} \\ CH & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ CH & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
